series.subject: CSEC Physics
series.goal: At least Grade II in CSEC Physics, May-June 2027, aiming for Grade I

episodes.title: Meet Kiara
episodes.summary: Meet Kiara Best, a Fifth Form student from St John, Barbados. She has 4,000 followers on TikTok, spends six and a half hours a day on her phone, and scored 41% in Form 4 physics. In her first session we set her goal, look at the whole exam, and run a diagnostic test.

lessons.title: Measurement, Errors and Significant Figures
lessons.why: For calculations: Formula, Fill, Finish: write the formula, fill in numbers with units, finish with a unit.

homework: Watch Lesson 3: Measurement, Errors and Significant Figures, with the phone in Granny's room.
Do item 6 again: the density of the block, with the formula, the numbers with units, and the answer with its unit. Bring it on Wednesday.
Turn on Do Not Disturb before our next session.

episodes.title: The Diagnosis and the Plan
episodes.summary: Kiara gets her diagnostic results: 14 out of 30. She is strong in waves, sound and light, from her video work. We find her five weaknesses, with evidence from her own answers, and build a 23-week plan.

lessons.title: Density
lessons.why: For calculations: Formula, Fill, Finish: write the formula, fill in numbers with units, finish with a unit.

homework: Watch Lesson 4: Density, in two focus blocks of 25 minutes.
Puzzle for Saturday: Granny's bucket holds 15 litres of water. Without a scale, how many kilograms of water is that?
One tick on the calendar for each focus block.

episodes.title: Formula, Fill, Finish
episodes.summary: Formula, Fill, Finish: one routine for every calculation. Kiara converts units with a metre cube, finds the weight of Granny's water buckets, and gets full marks on an exam-style density question.

lessons.title: Graphs, Best-Fit Lines and Gradients
lessons.why: For graphs: Label every axis 'quantity / unit'.

homework: Watch Lesson 2: Graphs, Best-Fit Lines and Gradients.
Ten calculations from Lessons 3 and 4, each in three lines. Photograph the page and send it before Tuesday.
Your 60-second video: after a focus block, no more than 20 minutes to film and edit, every fact checked against the lesson.
